content.value_statement: Bulk RNA-seq differential expression requires careful count preparation, design selection, and result interpretation. This skill guides PyDESeq2 workflows from input checks to tested genes, plots, and saved results.
actual_capabilities: Prepare count matrices and metadata for PyDESeq2 sample-by-gene input.
Build single-factor and multi-factor DESeq2 design formulas.
Run Wald tests with contrasts and adjusted p-value interpretation.
Apply optional log fold change shrinkage for ranking and plots.
Guide volcano plots, MA plots, and quality checks.
Use the bundled CLI script to export CSV, pickle, and plot files.
limitations: It targets bulk RNA-seq data, not single-cell differential expression.
It assumes PyDESeq2 and Python dependencies are installed.
It cannot replace experimental design review by a biostatistician.
Large datasets may require local compute resources and memory planning.

use_cases.title: Run a Treated Versus Control Study
use_cases.description: Plan a standard PyDESeq2 workflow from count files to significant gene lists.

use_cases.title: Control Batch Effects
use_cases.description: Design a multi-factor model that adjusts for batch while testing the condition effect.

use_cases.title: Move DESeq2 Workflows to Python
use_cases.description: Translate common DESeq2 analysis steps into a Python-based PyDESeq2 pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Two-Group Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PyDESeq2 to compare treated versus control samples. My files are counts.csv and metadata.csv. Explain data orientation and first checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Batch Adjustment
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PyDESeq2 workflow for counts.csv and metadata.csv with design batch plus condition. Use condition treated versus control.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Ranked Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PyDESeq2 result table. Identify significant genes using adjusted p-value below 0.05 and explain volcano plot thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Reproducible CLI Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a command and analysis checklist for scripts/run_deseq2_analysis.py with plots, LFC shrinkage, and saved outputs.

output_examples.input: Compare treated and control samples with count and metadata CSV files.
output_examples.output: A stepwise plan that checks sample alignment, filters low-count genes, runs PyDESeq2, and summarizes significant genes.

output_examples.input: Interpret a result table after a Wald test.
output_examples.output: A concise interpretation of adjusted p-values, log2 fold changes, upregulated genes, downregulated genes, and recommended plots.
A recommended design formula, contrast explanation, confounding checks, and export guidance for result tables and plots.

best_practices: Confirm count matrices are samples by genes before constructing the dataset.
Filter low-count genes before fitting the model.
Use adjusted p-values, not raw p-values, for significance calls.
anti_patterns: Do not use normalized counts as input to PyDESeq2.
Do not ignore missing metadata or sample name mismatches.
Do not rank genes by raw p-value alone.

faq.question: Does this skill run PyDESeq2 directly?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance and includes a script. Execution depends on the local Python environment and installed dependencies.

faq.question: What input format does it expect?
faq.answer: PyDESeq2 expects samples by genes counts and sample metadata with matching sample names.

faq.question: Can it handle batch effects?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a multi-factor design such as batch plus condition when metadata supports it.

faq.question: Does it support single-cell RNA-seq?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is for bulk RNA-seq count data.

faq.question: What outputs can the script save?
faq.answer: It can save result tables, significant gene tables, sorted results, pickled datasets, and optional plots.

faq.question: How should significance be reported?
faq.answer: Report adjusted p-values and log2 fold changes. Use raw p-values only as supporting information.
